content:
Yesterday we saw the tassels of the New Creation, the many reminders that call us to look and remember and obey. But all of this becomes useless if it remains only a beautiful interpretation. The real question is: how do we actually practise it? Numbers 15 gives us the answer. Yahweh wanted Israel to interrupt the movement from seeing, to desiring, to wandering, to sinning, by remembering His Word. And the New Creation must learn the very same discipline, for our eyes wander, our thoughts wander, our hands wander, our feet wander, and our desires wander. Therefore, we must train ourselves to remember before we act.

Paul says, "We have the mind of Christ" (1 Corinthians 2:16). To have the mind of Christ means that, instead of allowing the old nature to control our reactions, the thoughts and ways of Christ increasingly govern us. Romans 12:2 describes this as being "transformed by the renewing of your mind." This does not happen accidentally. It becomes a daily practice. Suppose our eyes begin looking at something impure. At that very moment, we must not allow the thought to keep travelling. We stop, and we remember: I belong to Christ.

We remember the cross. We remember the blood. We remember our baptism. And then we deliberately turn our eyes away. Job said, "I have made a covenant with my eyes" (Job 31:1). Suppose our feet begin taking us somewhere we know will weaken our walk. Before going further, we remember: where am I going? Would Christ lead me here? I have already left Egypt, so why am I walking back toward it? And then we turn around.

Suppose our hands are about to do something dishonest, harmful, or selfish. We remember, "Whatever you do, do all to the glory of God" (1 Corinthians 10:31), and we ask ourselves: can these hands, which belong to Christ, do this for His glory? If not, we stop. And suppose anger enters our thoughts. Someone has hurt us, and immediately the old man begins preparing an answer.
Before the tongue speaks, we remember Christ. How did He respond?What has He forgiven in me? What would the New Creation say here?Instead of allowing the old mind to finish its thought, we interrupt it with the Word. And that is exactly where Scripture becomes our daily tassel,for David said, "Your word I have hidden in my heart, that I might not sin against You" (Psalm 119:11). We cannot remember a Word we have never placed in our minds. So, if we want this practice to succeed, we must continually fill ourselves with Scripture. When tempted by anxiety,we remember a promise. When tempted by anger, we remember Christ's command. When tempted by lust, we remember holiness. When tempted by pride, we remember the cross. When tempted to return to the world,we remember our baptism. And when discouraged, we look again to Christ.

And slowly, something begins to change. At first, perhaps we only remember after we have already sinned. Then, as we grow, we begin to remember while we are being tempted. And finally, through continual practice, we begin to remember before we act. That is spiritual maturity. The mind is being trained. This is why Paul says we are "bringing every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ" (2 Corinthians 10:5). Notice those words, every thought. We capture it before the thought becomes a word, before the word becomes an action, before the action becomes a habit, and before the habit becomes our character. We capture the thought and bring it to Christ.

We can even build simple daily habits of remembrance. When we wake, we remember, I belong to Christ today. When we open the Scripture, we ask Yahweh to place His commandments within our minds. When temptation appears, we pause before responding. When we do something, we give thanks. When we remember our baptism, we remember that the old life was left behind. When we partake of the bread and the cup, we consciously remember Christ's body and blood. And before sleep, we examine the day: where did my eyes wander? Where did my thoughts wander? Where did my feet wander?

And where did Yahweh help me overcome? This is not empty religious routine. It is the training of the mind. Eventually the reminder no longer needs to hang physically from our clothing, because the Word is increasingly written upon the heart. The outward tassel pointed Israel back to Yahweh's command;the New Creation is being renewed inwardly, so that the mind of Christ increasingly governs our decisions.

Then the words of Numbers 15:39-40 become very precious, "That you may remember and do all My commandments and be holy for your God." That is the goal. Not merely remembering verses. Not merely knowing doctrine.

Not merely looking at Christian symbols. But rather this: look, remember, obey, and be holy. Our heart and our eyes can still wander, and so throughout every day we must keep bringing our minds back to Christ. When the eyes wander, remember. When the hands are tempted, remember. When the feet begin moving toward Egypt, remember. When the thoughts become impure, remember. When anger rises, remember. We look to Christ, we remember the cross and His precious blood, we remember our baptism, and we remember Him in the bread and the cup. Then we bring that thought under the obedience of Christ and choose accordingly. And if we practise this again and again, remembering will increasingly come before acting. The mind that once naturally followed the old man is renewed to think according to Christ. This is how the New Creation learns, day after day, to look, to remember, to obey, and to be holy unto Yahweh.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our Father, who renews the mind and writes Your Word upon the heart,
Teach us to remember before we act, and to interrupt every wandering thought with Your truth.

Help us to store Your Word in our hearts, that we might not sin against You.

Make us quick to capture every thought and bring it into the obedience of Christ.

Train our minds, day after day, until remembering comes before acting.

Let us look, remember, obey, and be holy unto You.

"Your word I have hidden in my heart, that I might not sin against You." Psalm 119:11

In Christ’s name we pray. Amen.
